questions.key_step: Count solutions of 2x+3tan x=pi on [-2pi,2pi]: branch-by-branch graph reading
questions.justification: Branch-by-branch graph count with two partial end branches; one familiar idea, careful but option-checkable.

questions.key_step: Homogenise 10sin^4+15cos^4=6 into a perfect square, then evaluate
questions.justification: Perfect-square trick then arithmetic with exponents; a few routine steps.

questions.key_step: Roots of 2x^2+cos(t)x-1: alpha^4+beta^4 as a function of cos^2
questions.justification: Symmetric functions plus a range of cos^2; routine chain.

questions.key_step: cot10cot70-1 = cos80/(sin10 sin70)
questions.justification: One compound-angle identity applied once.

questions.key_step: Telescoping 1/(sin sin) via cot differences, 13 terms with a period shift
questions.justification: Same telescoping idea as the L4 numerical anchor but single-correct and much shorter (no heavy numerics).

questions.key_step: sinx=cos^2x implies tanx=cosx; expression becomes 2(sinx+sin^2x)^3
questions.justification: Two substitutions and a cube recognition.

questions.key_step: cos t cos(60-t)cos(60+t)=cos3t/4; list solutions of cos3t=1/2 and add
questions.justification: Known identity, then a modest listing of six solutions.

questions.key_step: tan(A+B)=tanC by simplifying surds; A+B acute
questions.justification: Algebra with surds, routine tan addition.

questions.key_step: Two right triangles at Q give sin(2pi/3-t)=5/a; solve for a^2
questions.justification: Needs the angle set-up (2pi/3 - theta) then a short algebra step; lighter than the anchor.

questions.key_step: f=1+2cos^2/(sin^4+cos^2); range [1,3] by AM-GM; GP sum
questions.justification: Range by AM-GM plus the cos=0 case, then a one-line GP sum.

questions.key_step: Factor the surd quadratic in cos; 4+4 solutions
questions.justification: One factorisation and standard counting.

questions.key_step: Quadratic in sin x with surd coefficients; count sin x=1/2 in [-2pi,5pi/2]
questions.justification: Surd factorisation plus counting over an interval of 4.5 half-periods.

questions.key_step: cos(15t/2)-cos(3t/2)=0 after product-to-sum; two families, subtract the overlap
questions.justification: Several identities chained and an overlap at 0 to avoid double counting.

questions.key_step: |sin2x|=8/pi^2 gives 4 solutions; modulus equation gives x=0,1,9,16; check disjointness
questions.justification: Two independent counts plus the overlap check; a slip in either changes the answer.

questions.key_step: Square 4cos-1=3sin, choose the root consistent with theta in [0,pi/4]
questions.justification: Standard squaring with root rejection and rationalisation.

questions.key_step: cos t=1/3; find least n for 7 solutions (n=13); sum k/2^k
questions.justification: Three stages: reduce to cos=1/3, count in order to get n, then an AGP sum.

questions.key_step: Divide by cos, square, reject extraneous root by sign of sec
questions.justification: Standard auxiliary-equation solve with one root to reject.

questions.key_step: cos^6-sin^6 factorisation makes LHS the constant 4; cubic with one real root
questions.justification: Identity-heavy simplification plus the trap of counting complex roots; options help.

questions.key_step: Equation collapses to sin x=2/3; third solution fixes n=5; quadratic roots negative
questions.justification: Simplify, count solutions to find n, then root location.

questions.key_step: 4cos^3+4cos^2+4cos=13 impossible since LHS<=12
questions.justification: One bounding insight; short.
